tools.name: search
tools.description: Find public MCP servers or coding agents by name, task, package coordinate or URL, using the same staged search as the website. Returns IDs for fetch.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Retrieve a public result from search. Every declared feature retains its source, collection date and explicit-empty indicator.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Compare two to four public entries. Missing observations remain separate from false and explicitly empty values. No safety or trust ranking.

tools.name: configure
tools.description: Generate a local or remote connection configuration template for one public MCP entry using tracevero’s existing rules. Does not install or execute anything. Secret values are never requested; placeholders need to be filled locally.

tools.name: plan_workflow
tools.description: Decompose a documented task and find API operations for existing apps. Shows uncovered steps, permission alternatives, costs and untested connector boundaries. Never executes the workflow.

tools.name: get_connection_options
tools.description: Inspect separate local and remote paths, declared secrets, documented authentication and verification limits for a public entry.

tools.name: validate_config
tools.description: Check JSON structure and Docker environment forwarding for a client. Submit a locally sanitized configuration, never live tokens. Returns redacted repairs; no installation or execution.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "configure" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search · Private data: configure, get_connection_options, validate_config · Public sink: validate_config · Destructive: configure.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search · Private data: configure, get_connection_options, validate_config · Public sink: validate_config · Destructive: configure

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
